in_hebrew.name: לידיה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם לידיה מגיע מהמילה העברית 'ליד' שפירושה שמחה או משמח, וקשור לנושא העבודה והפולחן לאל. הוא מופיע בברית החדשה ומתייחס לאישה מאזור תראקיה שהייתה מקבלת פולחן נוצרי.

in_greek.name: Λυδία
in_greek.long_meaning: Τὸ ὄνομα Λυδία προέρχεται ἀπὸ τὴν περιοχή Λυδία στὴν Μικρά Ἀσία. Ἡ Λυδία αὐτῆς τῆς περιοχῆς ἦταν γνωστή ὡς πλουσία καὶ ἐπιφανής. Ἡ Λυδία στὴν Καινή Διαθήκη ἦταν μίας ἀπὸ τὶς πρώτες γυναῖκες στὴν Φιλίπποι πού ἐπεβλήθη εἰς τὸ Χριστιανισμὸ ὑπὸ τὸν Παῦλον.

in_latin.name: Lydia
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Lydia originem trahit ex Lydia regione Asiae Minoris. In Novo Testamento, Lydia fuit mulier dives et hospitalis, prima Philippis ad fidem Christianam conversa per Paulum apostolum.

in_english.name: Lidija
in_english.meaning: Beautiful, industrious, and happy, derived from ancient regions
in_english.long_meaning: The name Lidija originates from the ancient region of Lydia in Asia Minor. It signifies beauty, industriousness, and happiness. In Christian tradition, Lidija is associated with Saint Lydia, a wealthy and pious businesswoman from Thyatira, converted by St. Paul in Philippi (Acts 16:14-15). The name symbolizes spiritual beauty, devotion, and entrepreneurial spirit. It is popular across Christian cultures for its historical and biblical significance.

biblical_reference.note: Lydia of Thyatira, a follower of Christ

data.cultural_impact: The name Lidija has a rich cultural history, as it is of ancient Hebrew origin and is embraced in both Eastern and Western Christian traditions. It has been passed down through generations, and is still used in many parts of Europe and beyond. Furthermore, it represents a devotion to God and the light of faith, which has been a source of comfort, inspiration, and strength for countless individuals throughout history.
data.spiritual_significance: Lidija is a name that speaks to the deep spiritual beliefs and values of those who bear it. The name is a constant reminder of the presence and power of God in our lives, and the importance of keeping our faith strong amidst life's challenges and uncertainties. It serves as a reminder of the light that God is, and the guidance and protection He provides to those who trust in Him.

historical_references.reference: According to Belarusian legend, Lidija was a Christian princess who ruled the lands of Polotsk and Novgorod in the 11th century. She is said to have converted the local population to Christianity, and is venerated as the patron saint of Polotsk and of Belarus.

Another reference to Lidija comes from the 15th century Polish chronicles, where she is mentioned as a daughter of Prince Włodzisław of Opole, who was married to Prince Sviatoslav of Polotsk around 1311. There is no evidence that Lidija actually ruled Polotsk or Novgorod, but she is mentioned as a Christian princess in Polish sources.

Lidija has gained popularity in recent years due to the trend of using Slavic and European names, as well as the growing interest in multicultural names. Additionally, baby names websites have seen an increase in searches for Lidija, reflecting its growing popularity as a modern name.
